summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a planned coil embolization of the renal artery to manage complications from a failed kidney transplant. Due to prior abdominal wall reconstruction, surgical removal was deemed high-risk, so a minimally invasive approach was chosen. The procedure was performed successfully without complications. Post-procedure, she remained on bedrest, ambulated without difficulty, and tolerated a regular diet. The transplant team recommended discontinuing Myfortic and initiating a short steroid taper, while continuing tacrolimus. She completed a scheduled hemodialysis session and had stable vital signs. Her warfarin was planned for restart post-discharge with INR monitoring. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions for incision care, activity, and follow-up with her nephrologist.
problems: Surgical operation with transplant of whole organ causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
